rubric.why: Identifies chlorophyll as the green pigment found in chloroplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying chlorophyll as a green pigment in the chloroplasts.

rubric.why: Explains that chlorophyll captures light energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chlorophyll absorbs or traps light energy.

rubric.why: Explains that light provides the energy for photosynthesis and that this energy is converted and stored in food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that light supplies energy for photosynthesis and 1 mark for explaining that light energy is converted into chemical energy stored in food.

rubric.why: States that light is required for photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that light is essential or necessary for photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Chlorophyll is the green pigment found in the chloroplasts of plant cells.
It absorbs or traps light energy from the Sun.
The absorbed light energy is converted into chemical energy and stored in the food produced.
Therefore, light is essential for photosynthesis, and chlorophyll enables the plant to capture its energy.

items.followUp: Why is a control group used in an experiment?

rubric.why: Identifies the control as a standard setup used for comparison with the experimental setup.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a control is the standard setup used for comparison with the experimental setup.

rubric.why: Explains that the tested factor is absent from the control while other conditions remain the same.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the tested factor is absent from the control and that other conditions are kept the same.

modelAnswer: A control is the standard setup in an experiment used for comparison with the experimental setup.
The tested factor is absent from the control, while other conditions are kept the same, so the effect of that factor can be identified.
